title: Implement RBAC v2 attenuation rules, KMS stamp validator, and audit HyperLog
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: - Adds RBAC v2 attenuation rules to constrain operator token privileges over time. - Introduces KMS stamp validator to assert key provenance and region/tenant binding. - Adds a compact audit HyperLog index to deduplicate high-throughput audit events. Rollout is gated behind rbacv2.attenuation.enabled feature flag.
description: Motivation: customers and internal auditors requested stronger mitigations for long-lived operator tokens and better assurance that KMS keys used for tenant encryption are region-bound and provable. Additionally, audit traffic growth for operator actions caused duplicate records and increased storage cost._This PR adds three coordinated pieces: (1) an RBAC v2 attenuation pipeline that reduces effective privileges for operator tokens over time and enforces per-tenant max-scope; (2) a KMS stamp validator that verifies an embedded provenance stamp (kms.provenance.v1) returned by key provisioning flows and rejects keys that do not assert tenant+region binding; (3) a compact audit HyperLog index used in the audit ingest path to dedupe repeated high-frequency operator events before long-term storage. Design notes: attenuation is implemented as a post-decision policy mutator in services/rbacv2/pdp so PDP responses are still auditable; we do not change decision APIs. Attenuation rules are policy-driven and configurable per-tenant via the existing policy service; defaults apply to operator tokens older than 24h. The KMS stamp validator is a small middleware in services/kms/stamp that validates a signed stamp and canonicalizes the key metadata used by the runtime. The audit HyperLog is a probabilistic dedup index (HyperLog-style) scoped by tenant+route+minute; entries beyond the configured threshold are collapsed into a single summarized event to reduce storage and improve alert signal-to-noise. Backwards compatibility: features are behind two feature flags (rbacv2.attenuation.enabled, audit.hyperlog.enabled) and default to off for existing clusters. Migration: we add a lightweight migration that creates the HyperLog schema table; it's designed to be idempotent. Security considerations: stamp validator rejects keys missing the kms.provenance.v1 envelope or with mismatched region claim; an allowlist exists for legacy keys during a 30-day migration window. Performance: HyperLog memory is bounded by implementation config, and attenuation logic is constant-time per decision. See performance section below. Checklist: [x] API contract documented in docs/security/kms-stamp.md. [x] Unit tests for attenuation rule interpreter. [x] Integration test for KMS stamp validation. [x] Integration test for audit dedupe path. [x] Feature flags added and wired to Console. [x] Helm values and operator manifests updated. Deployment notes: enable the flags in staging and monitor audit_dedupe_rate and rbac_attenuation_rejections for 72h. If the KMS stamp validator causes unexpected rejections, use the operator k8s rollout to flip kms.stamp.allowlist=true for affected namespaces. Related tickets: ENG-3721, SEC-120, SUP-4598.

review_comments: Jonah Rees: Performance ok on unit runs but we need an estimate on memory growth for HyperLog in worst-case tenants. Please add a helm tunable and a hard cap.

Mei Chen: KMS stamp schema looks good. Question: how do we handle cross-region key rotation? Reply: we introduced kms.stamp.allowlist for migration and a rotation policy that requires new stamps to be minted; docs updated to describe operator flow.

discussion_summary: Review focused on three areas: measurable bounds for HyperLog memory, safe migration for legacy KMS keys, and ensuring attenuation is auditable and reversible during rollout. Team agreed on feature flags and a 30-day allowlist strategy. Performance tests were run on staging with representative traffic and showed <2% p50 latency regression on PDP calls when attenuation enabled.
risk_assessment: Medium. The KMS stamp validator can cause operational impact if legacy keys are not migrated; mitigations include an allowlist and operator rollback. HyperLog dedupe reduces storage costs but could hide noisy events if misconfigured; default dedupe thresholds are conservative.
test_plan: Unit tests added for attenuation interpreter and stamp validator. Integration tests added that spin up kms-mock and exercise stamp success/failure paths and audit dedupe logic. Staging rollout will enable flags for 72h with metric collection (rbac_attenuation_rejections, audit_dedupe_rate, kms_stamp_rejects).
deploy_notes: Feature flags: rbacv2.attenuation.enabled=false, audit.hyperlog.enabled=false, kms.stamp.allowlist=true by default. Staged rollout: enable attenuation in a single region, monitor 72h; then enable HyperLog dedupe; finally enable strict stamp validation and move allowlist to false. Operators can toggle helm value compliance.kms.allowlist=true to temporarily permit legacy keys.
